findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:35 — [P3][confidence 100][advisory: wrong-shape,coupling] Verbatim code: `.panel { position: relative; margin-left: auto; @include order(3); }`. Definite failure: replacing the selector's layout-independent `float: right` with flex-item-only alignment couples this shared `.panel` rule to an unstated requirement that `.panel` be a direct child of `.contents`. Trigger: render the non-Ember/noscript header, whose `.panel` is nested inside `.row` rather than being a flex item. Failure mode and consequence: `margin-left: auto` and `order` do not participate in the ancestor `.contents` flex formatting context, so the login panel loses right alignment and stacks under/alongside the title according to normal `.row` flow. Strongest rebuttal: the Ember header's `.panel` is a direct flex item and renders correctly; it loses because this selector owns both header implementations while only one DOM shape satisfies the new contract, so the change breaks the other implementer and leaks the Ember hierarchy into shared CSS.

app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:121 — [P3][confidence 100][advisory: simplification] Verbatim code: `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. Definite failure: the shared `align-items` mixin emits a legacy compatibility branch that no IE or Edge flexbox implementation recognizes; the implemented IE 10/11 property is the preceding `-ms-flex-align`. Trigger: every `@include align-items(...)` added here expands this declaration. Failure mode and consequence: the branch is always discarded, adds dead CSS to every consumer, and falsely advertises an additional Microsoft compatibility path in the central cross-browser contract. Strongest rebuttal: it is harmless because `-ms-flex-align` already provides the intended behavior; it loses because that proves this line has zero behavior and zero fallback value. Simplification: delete exactly line 121, `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, with no replacement and no consumer updates.

docs/tasks/task-001.md:1 — P2 confidence 100; verbatim `# Task: Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins`; trigger: accepting this task as done; failure: the task defines no baseline, measured metric, target threshold, browser matrix, or visual acceptance criterion, so there is no determinate condition under which the stated optimization is complete; strongest author rebuttal: the requested review can infer success from the CSS diff, but that loses because a syntactic conversion to flexbox establishes neither a performance gain nor preserved layout across supported browsers.

docs/metareview/context/mrv-20260911-021126013196000-task-done-task-001-2a8bd7a9-context.md:233 — P2 confidence 100; verbatim `No external validation evidence supplied.`; trigger: evaluating the completed performance optimization; failure: the submission provides no before/after performance measurement and no rendered responsive or cross-browser verification, leaving the sole stated performance requirement and the layout-preservation requirement unverified; strongest author rebuttal: static inspection is sufficient for a stylesheet-only change, but that loses because static inspection cannot measure layout performance or demonstrate rendering preservation.

app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:117 — P2 confidence 100; verbatim `@mixin align-items($alignment) {`; trigger: Gecko versions that consume the mixins' `display: -moz-box` fallback render `.d-header .contents`, `.small-action`, or `.badge-wrapper.bullet`; failure: the mixin omits the required sibling declaration `-moz-box-align: $alignment`, so those fallback containers retain the legacy default alignment instead of the requested center or baseline alignment; strongest author rebuttal: unprefixed `align-items` covers Firefox, but that loses because the code explicitly supports the earlier `-moz-box` model whose alignment property is `-moz-box-align`.

app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:263 — P2, confidence 100, blocking: verbatim `.small-action { @include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);` plus `.small-action-desc { padding: 0 1.5%;` and `p { margin: 0; }`; trigger: rendering any small-action row in a topic after accepting the stated human objective `Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins`; failure mode: this iteration changes a non-header topic row from the established float/block layout to flex and removes its vertical spacing, so the delivered artifact silently substitutes a broader topic-body redesign for the header-only objective without explicit human acceptance.

app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:263 — P2, confidence 100: the verbatim change `.small-action { @include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);` (together with `.small-action-desc { padding: 0 1.5%;` and removed paragraph spacing) is unrelated expansion beyond the stated header-layout intent; when a topic renders any small-action post it changes that post row from the established float/block layout to flex and removes its vertical spacing, producing a user-visible topic-body redesign with no requirement traceability, and the strongest rebuttal—that reusing the new flexbox mixins improves layout consistently—loses because `.small-action` is outside `.d-header` and deleting this entire topic-post hunk leaves the requested header conversion intact.

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:117 — P2 confidence 100; verbatim `@mixin align-items($alignment) {`; trigger: Gecko versions that consume the mixins' `display: -moz-box` fallback render `.d-header .contents`, `.small-action`, or `.badge-wrapper.bullet`; failure: the mixin omits the required sibling declaration `-moz-box-align: $alignment`, so those fallback containers retain the legacy default alignment instead of the requested center or baseline alignment; strongest author rebuttal: unprefixed `align-items` covers Firefox, but that loses because the code explicitly supports the earlier `-moz-box` model whose alignment property is `-moz-box-align`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the `@mixin align-items($alignment)` mixin at lines 117-123 includes `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, `-ms-align-items`, and `align-items`, but does NOT include `-moz-box-align`. Since the `@mixin flexbox()` includes `display: -moz-box` as a fallback (line 99), and the `@mixin inline-flex()` includes `display: -moz-inline-box` (line 107), older Firefox versions using the `-moz-box` display model would need `-moz-box-align` to properly align items. The mixin is missing this vendor prefix, which is a legitimate bug for consistency with the other flexbox mixins that do include Mozilla prefixes.
